case_title: Mariappan v. State Rep. by Inspector of Police
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; IPC s.304 Part-I
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC, acquitted accused nos. 2 and 3
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were involved in a heated verbal argument. During the altercation, the accused stabbed the victim multiple times with a soori-knife, while another accused used a spade handle but did not inflict injuries. The victim was taken to a hospital where he was pronounced dead. The police registered a case under Sections 302 and 324 of the IPC. The investigation collected bloodstained evidence, a murder weapon, and forensic reports. The trial court convicted the accused based on the testimonies of witnesses, the recovery of the weapon, and forensic evidence. The accused was acquitted due to lack of conclusive evidence. The high court confirmed the conviction, but the supreme court converted the conviction under Section 302 to Section 304 Part-I with a sentence of 10 years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 50,000.
